history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: No published travel, tourism, or temple source documents a specific 'Hanuman Temple' in Mokokchung town; the identity, exact location, age, and history of this shrine could not be verified, so this entry is provisional (verify). The town-level Hindu temple listing for Mokokchung (onefivenine.com) records only four temples - Sarvajanik Gorkha Mandir (Arkong), Laxminarayn Templ, Durga Mandir (NH-61) and Bishnu Mandir - none of which is a named Hanuman temple. The only Hanuman Temple with any map/web record near Mokokchung district is at 'National Highway 61, Amguri, Assam' (onefivenine.com Longchem/Yajang-C listing), which is across the state border in Assam's Sivasagar district, roughly 50 km north of Mokokchung town, and must not be conflated with the CSV row. No CSV town/district/state correction is needed (Mokokchung, Mokokchung district, Nagaland); coordinates are the Mokokchung town centroid (verify). Mokokchung is the cultural heart of the Ao Naga people and is overwhelmingly Christian; Hindu shrines here are small community-serving temples of the non-tribal (largely Gorkha) population.

name: Mokokchung Hanuman Temple
town_description: Mokokchung is the cultural heart of the Ao Naga people in the northern hills of Nagaland and the headquarters of Mokokchung district, sitting at about 1,325 m elevation on NH-2. Largely Christian (the Ao Nagas were evangelised from 1872), it has a small non-tribal Hindu population (largely Gorkha) served by a handful of small temples in and around town. Nearby attractions include the villages of Ungma, Longkhum and Chuchuyimlang, the Langpangkong caves and the Moatsu festival (May).
tradition: Vaishnavism (presumed; verify - Hanuman is worshipped as a Rama-bhakta devotee-deity)
